### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/driver-memory`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-executor.ts`, `packages/verify/README.md`, `packages/verify/src/dashboard-window.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via MemoryAnalyticsService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-executor.ts`, `packages/verify/README.md`, `packages/verify/src/dashboard-window.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 06dbc4e59d1a37011114441317b6f918386cd690` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d94062790db8a4c37826a764690b39ae4be49908` — the merge of head `8927fbc43cbdb646f0578cc8f0967a3672b569dd` into base `06dbc4e59d1a37011114441317b6f918386cd690`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d94062790db8a4c37826a764690b39ae4be49908 && git checkout d94062790db8a4c37826a764690b39ae4be49908
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 06dbc4e59d1a37011114441317b6f918386cd690 8927fbc43cbdb646f0578cc8f0967a3672b569dd && git checkout -B drift-repro 06dbc4e59d1a37011114441317b6f918386cd690 && git merge --no-ff 8927fbc43cbdb646f0578cc8f0967a3672b569dd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 06dbc4e59d1a37011114441317b6f918386cd690
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 06dbc4e59d1a37011114441317b6f918386cd690` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## `check-empty-changeset` is red by design on this PR: a DELIBERATE CORRECTION of a pending release note

- **Gate:** `node scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs --base origin/main`, the foreign changeset rule (ruling D on #17712). Measured at head `da95e4e8e`: exit 1.
- **Note it names:** `.changeset/pre/15953-verify-dashboard-window-family.md`. It is on the merge base, and this PR did not add it.
- **What changed under it:** this PR closes the rolling `last_N_days` windows of `DATE_RANGE_PRESET_MACRO_WINDOWS` on `{today}`. `@objectstack/verify`'s dashboard-window family therefore hands the dataset door `{ $gte: '{7_days_ago}', $lte: '{today}' }` for `last_7_days`. The note's sentence quoted `{ $gte: '{7_days_ago}' }`, which this PR makes false.
- **What was done:** only that quoted window was corrected, in place. The note's frontmatter (63 bytes) is byte-identical.
- **Why it is not restored:** the note is pending. The `18.0.0-next.0` release consumed it into `.changeset/pre/`, and it is aggregated into the stable `18.0.0` notes at pre exit. Restoring it from the base would publish the false sentence.
- **Confirmation:** claim amendment 6142517145 on #23170 names this edit, and the same-head contract-tier review is the written confirmation.

The gate's verdict lines, verbatim:

```text
This PR changes a changeset it did not add:

   .changeset/pre/15953-verify-dashboard-window-family.md
     present on the merge base and CHANGED by this PR -- this is somebody else's release note

  DELIBERATE CORRECTION -- your change may have made this PENDING release note false, and you rewrote it in the same stroke. Remedy: do NOT restore it -- say so on the PR and get it confirmed; restoring it from the base would put the false sentence back.
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Local-runs: none

**Inputs read.** Card #23170: body and all 7 comments (6139344728 triage, 6139488818 claim, 6141817295 and 6142517145 amendments, 6142485762 and 6143940540 `os-dev-report`, 6143978957 seat ACCEPT — read, not used as evidence). PR #23208: body, both PR comments (6141838681 docs-drift, 6143910790 gate-and-reason), the 21-file list, and the net diff against `main` at the head (243 added / 170 deleted; `git diff` from merge base `75cada0ea` to the head lists the same 21 files). The head's 52 check-runs. Every head read was addressed by the 40-hex sha (`git show da95e4e8e8f1ce7d21fe425fdc4eceabe3341dab:PATH`, `git grep PATTERN da95e4e8e8f1ce7d21fe425fdc4eceabe3341dab -- PATHS`); `FETCH_HEAD` was never read for content (consulted once, by `rev-parse`, to confirm my own fetch had landed on that sha). `origin/main` was fetched twice (`01a3421f4`, then `197fbe2c0` for the final sweep — it moved between them) and read as `origin/main:PATH`. The installed `@changesets/*` were read from the sibling checkout's pnpm store (`/home/user/objectstack-issue-23147/node_modules/.pnpm/`: cli 3.0.3, read 1.0.1, assemble-release-plan 7.0.0, apply-release-plan 8.1.1, matching the root `package.json` pin `^3.0.3`) because `/home/user/objectstack` carries no `node_modules`.

**Check-runs on the head** (read 2026-10-13, every run `completed`, none in progress). `Check Changeset`: failure, three times (one per PR event, 09:33 / 10:50 / 10:55) — the designed red. Job 115260066110's steps: 11 `Require a changeset` success; 12 `Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset` failure, its annotation naming `.changeset/pre/15953-verify-dashboard-window-family.md` with the two-class remedy text verbatim; 13 `Require an ADR-0087 disposition` success; 15 `Guard against accidental major bumps` success (so the `Clause-②` line parsed). Every other run that ran: success — `Test Core` and its six shards, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, every `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` lane, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, the four claim guards, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`. Skipped by path or event: `Temporal Conformance`, the `Dogfood Regression Gate` matrix, `Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI` (`ci.yml:2214` skips it on `pull_request` and `merge_group` by design; `packages/cli/test/verify-dashboard-windows.test.ts` pins no window literal, so nothing there goes red on `main`'s full run), `Packed-tarball smoke`. The PR's `mergeable_state: unstable` is that one non-required red.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The table and its type — right.** `readonly [start: string, end: string]` holds for all 13 rows: each is two wrapped macro tokens, and `date-range-presets.test.ts` pins every token's membership in the macro vocabulary. Head readers of `DATE_RANGE_PRESET_MACRO_WINDOWS` outside tests: `packages/spec/src/data/date-range-presets.ts:166` (the refusal), `packages/lint/src/validate-preset-comparands.ts:300` (the verdict), `packages/verify/src/dashboard-window.ts:628` (the family's condition), `packages/core/src/utils/analytics-date-range.ts` (docblock only; its own `PRESET_WINDOW_TOKENS` states ends in the stops-before spelling), and the generated `api-surface/data.json:158` / `export-origins/data.json:155`, which record the name only — so the narrowing moves no generated artifact, consistent with the 21-file list. No reader on the head branches on `end === null` any more (`filter-lowering.ts:345`'s `end === null` is a `$between` comparand element, unrelated). `verify`'s `to ? …` at :629, `end ? …` at :547 and `$lte === undefined` at :556 / :561 are dead arms the closed table never feeds. objectui at its local HEAD: 0 readers of the table; its `packages/core/src/utils/dashboard-filters.ts:176-178` already lowers the three to `{N_days_ago}` through `{today}`. The changeset's sentence "A reader that compared `end` with `null` still compiles" is TRUE under the root `tsconfig.json` (`strict: true`, inherited by spec): TypeScript permits `===` against `null` on any operand type (the comparability relation special-cases a nullable comparand, so no TS2367); the branch is dead, not ill-typed.

**(b) One extent at every face — right.** Spec: `$between: ['{N_days_ago}', '{today}']`, whose bare-day maximum covers the whole day (the calendar-day rule the table's docblock and `filter.zod.ts:361` state). Verify: hands `{ $gte: '{N_days_ago}', $lte: '{today}' }` (`dashboard-window.ts:628-629`) and judges by inclusive day. Core: `['N_days_ago', 'tomorrow']` with `endExclusive: true` (`analytics-date-range.ts:145-147`, `:185-192`), both bounds the reference zone's midnight. Memory driver: `parseDateRangeString` calls the shared resolver and compiles `$lt: end` for an exclusive end (`memory-analytics.ts:1198-1247`, `:2253-2255`). Native SQL: shared resolver at `:1296`, `$lt` at `:1323`. ObjectQL strategy: shared resolver at `:2069`, `$lt` at `:2076-2078`. Dataset executor: `lowerDatasetCompareDateRange` (`:645-652`) then `inclusiveCalendarDayWindow` reads the exclusive end, so the last day is today. Preview: `lowerPreviewDateRange` (`:618-625`), shared resolver. Every face: from the first instant of the day N days ago through the last instant of today, in the reference timezone — the console's extent. No face on the head selects another extent. Pins: spec (the rows, day counts 8 / 31 / 91, the today−5 / today+5 measurement, the `$between` prescription); core (all 13 `endExclusive`; the rolling end equals `today`'s end in every sweep zone; today±5; a later-today row inside; the #17341 sweep now over all 13); lint (verdict text verbatim); service-analytics (preview: last instant of today inside, tomorrow's first instant out; executor: `[2026-08-10T00:00:00.000Z, 2026-09-10T00:00:00.000Z, true]`, `previousPeriod` 31 days); driver-memory (the conformance kit holds every face to the shared resolver); verify (`dashboard-window.test.ts:190` pins the handed condition; the family proves counts under every preset on first / last day and a day either side, never after today). Not pinned anywhere: a future-dated row at the HTTP door (`POST /analytics/dataset/query`, today+5) — the dev declares it NOT MEASURED; the door lowers through the pinned strategies and the pinned bare-day rule, so the declaration is accepted; a pin there is a follow-up, not a blocker.

**(c) Rows selected — judged in ②.** Neither an accept-set narrowing nor a widening; a bug-class correction of query semantics toward the one ruled extent.

**(d) Shipped sentences — one FALSE sentence remains on the head.** Verified TRUE in context on the head: every sentence of `.changeset/23170-rolling-presets-close-on-today.md` (the before-state, the card's measurement, the three rows, the type and its compile claim, the `$between` prescription and its old `$gte` form, the `tomorrow` / `endExclusive: true` arm, the array arm keeping `$lte` at every face, and the "add `$lte: '{today}'`" advice — a bare-day `$lte` covers the whole day); `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts:2299-2301` (`$between`, first day through last, rolling last day `{today}`); `packages/core/src/utils/analytics-date-range-conformance.ts:160`, `:188-190`, `:221`; `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:2035-2036` and `packages/verify/README.md:161` (both match what `dashboard-window.ts:628-629` hands the door); `native-sql-strategy.ts:1319-1321`; `objectql-strategy.ts:2073-2077`; `dataset-executor.ts:668-673` (its later "[#18245]" paragraph still says the ten calendar presets open and close at the zone's midnight — true, merely no longer the whole set); `memory-analytics.ts:2240-2242`; `dashboard-window.ts:22-23`, `:554`; the two driver-memory test comments; `.changeset/pre/15953:15`. Sweep of `packages/` and `content/docs/` on the head for "end(s) at NOW", "bound is NOW", "REACHES", "`$gte`-only", "open arm", "no upper bound", "rolling end open", "end: null", "endBefore: null", "endExclusive: false", and every `{7|30|90_days_ago}` spelling in single AND double quotes: every hit is an authored macro-filter example (`date-macros.zod.ts:16`, `content/docs/references/data/date-macros.mdx:20`, `skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md:133`, the lint positive control at `validate-preset-comparands.ts:91`, test fixtures), an unrelated sense of "open arm" / "no upper bound", the array arm (`endExclusive: false` at `memory-analytics.ts:1198`, `dataset-executor.ts:651`, `preview-evaluator.ts:632`), release-owned CHANGELOG history (`packages/verify/CHANGELOG.md:38`, `packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md:78`, the next.0 rendering of the old sentence), or the counterfactual at `analytics-date-range.ts:64` — EXCEPT one: `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.filter-preset-ordering-comparand-refused.ts:31-33`, the ADR-0087 semantic entry's `replacement`: "the date-macro window the preset already means — { $gte: "{30_days_ago}" } for last_30_days, { $between: ["{week_start}", "{week_end}"] } for this_week, and so on (the rejection names the exact window per preset; DATE_RANGE_PRESET_MACRO_WINDOWS in @objectstack/spec/data is the table)". On the head the rejection names `{ $between: ['{30_days_ago}', '{today}'] }` for `last_30_days`, so the entry now prescribes, as the preset's own window and as what the rejection names, the exact `$gte`-only form this card retires. It ships: `spec-changes.ts:259` projects `replacement` into `spec-changes.json`, `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts:790`, `:800` prints "surface → replacement" to an upgrading consumer, and the entry is in `packages/spec/src/**`, the path leg under review. The dev's sweep used the single-quote spelling and missed the double-quote one. This entry has been corrected in place twice before, each with a spec changeset sentence (`packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md:21195` `9df3934`, `:21210` `6696056`), so an in-place edit is the established remedy. Sweep of `origin/main` past the merge base (`75cada0ea` to `197fbe2c0`: 13 commits, 120 files, nine new changesets): the lines `main` added carry no sentence of this class — no `DATE_RANGE_PRESET_MACRO_WINDOWS`, rolling-end, `N_days_ago`, `end: null`, `endExclusive: false` or `$gte`-only spelling landed after the merge base, and the only path `main` and this PR both touch is `rule-explanations.ts`, at hunks 598-670 against this PR's 2296.

**(e) The `end === null` branch removal in lint — truly unreachable on the merged head.** `presetComparandVerdict` reads `end` only from the table (`validate-preset-comparands.ts:300`), the table is `Readonly` with `end: string`, and `git grep` finds no site assigning into it. Taking the proof on the merged head rather than on `origin/main` was right: on `origin/main` the arm is still live.

**(f) DELIBERATE CORRECTION — CONFIRMED.** On the head `@objectstack/verify`'s family hands the dataset door `{ $gte: '{7_days_ago}', $lte: '{today}' }` for `last_7_days` (`dashboard-window.ts:628-629`, pinned at `dashboard-window.test.ts:190`), which is exactly the corrected quoted window at `.changeset/pre/15953-verify-dashboard-window-family.md:15`; that line is the file's only change, and the frontmatter (`'@objectstack/verify': minor`, `'@objectstack/cli': minor`; 63 bytes with both fences) is byte-identical to the merge base. Mechanism, read from the installed packages: `@changesets/read` 1.0.1 `dist/index.mjs:29` enumerates `.changeset/pre/*.md` as ids prefixed `pre/`; `@changesets/assemble-release-plan` 7.0.0 `dist/index.mjs:328` drops `pre/` ids only while `preState.mode !== "exit"`, so at `changeset pre exit` + `version` every consumed `pre/` note is aggregated into the stable `18.0.0` release notes; `@changesets/apply-release-plan` 8.1.1 `dist/index.mjs:301-313` is what renamed it into `pre/` at the `18.0.0-next.0` cut. `release.yml:503`, `:763` counts `pre/*.md` as pending stock, consistently. `Check Changeset` runs on `pull_request` only (`pr-automation.yml:41-42`; `merge_group` appears in 15 other workflows, not this one) and is not a required context (`pr-automation.yml:710-712`), so the designed red blocks no queue build. PR comment 6143910790 is accurate sentence by sentence (gate and exit code, the file's presence on the merge base, what changed, the 63-byte frontmatter, the pending-note mechanism, the confirmation route). The correction is CONFIRMED as right in substance; because this record is FAIL on other grounds, it is not the same-head PASS the queue needs — the record on the next head restates this confirmation.

### ② Semver level

Changeset: `@objectstack/spec: patch`, `@objectstack/core: patch`, body carrying `Clause-②: no (no accept set widens …)`; the launch-window guard (step 15) and the ADR-0087 disposition gate (step 13) both ran green on the head.

- **No accept set moves.** The save door refuses the same inputs as before (only its prescription text changes); the lint rule flags the same inputs; core's resolver accepts the same 13 names and refuses the same strings. The type narrowing `end: string | null` → `end: string` on a `Readonly` const tightens a reader's guarantee, is compile-compatible for every reader (including one comparing to `null`), and is not an accept set.
- **What the rows do.** At the analytics preset arm the three rolling windows now include later-today rows they dropped (end moves from the reference instant to tomorrow's midnight); relative to the old prescription an authored window now excludes future-dated rows. That is a correction of query semantics toward one ruled extent on a `bug` card — not a Clause-② `yes` (no new key on a published payload, no validator widened) and not a `(narrowing)` breaking change (no accepted input refused, no export removed, nothing authorable retired). `patch` + `patch` is right; `minor` would be owed only for an added surface, `major` only for a refused input or a removed export — neither happens. **No ADR-0087 marker is owed**: nothing authorable is removed and no breaking level is declared; the `null` arm was a const's value shape, not an authorable key. In pre mode every package of the `fixed` group bumps to `18.0.0-next.1` regardless; the level governs only the CHANGELOG section.
- **Owed attribution, missing:** `@objectstack/lint` ships a changed `os explain filter-preset-comparand` paragraph and `@objectstack/verify` ships a changed README (in its `files`); AGENTS.md rule 3 ("Add a changeset for anything that publishes") and precedent `9fbabd76a` (an explain-text fix carried `@objectstack/lint: patch`) put a `patch` line for each in the changeset. Version-neutral under `fixed`; fix in the same round.
- `Clause-②:` **no** — right.

### ③ Boundary flags

Report 6142485762: (1) stale PR body — rewritten in round 2; the head body carries both amendment sections and the designed-red section: answered. (2) model-named trailer amended before push — the four branch commits carry only `Claude-Session` and `Co-authored-by: Claude`: verified. (3) spec / core / lint `repo` vitest projects not run locally, declared to CI — `Test Core` and six shards green on the head: answered. (4) service-analytics / verify suites narrowed to one file in round 1 — round 2 ran service-analytics in full; verify ran its one file; CI green: answered. (5) a derived-gate shell loop stopped by a safety check, the two gates run directly — procedural, no effect. (6) `origin/main` not merged in round 1 — merged in round 2 (`2a2a6cf0c`); `main` has since moved 13 commits (tip `197fbe2c0` at my last fetch), overlapping this diff only in `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts` at hunks 598-670 against this PR's 2296, so the queue's rebuild merges clean. Open question (text made false, a–g) — answered A by the seat and executed; each item verified true on the head in ①(d).

Report 6143940540: (1) three sweep edits beyond the six (`native-sql-strategy.ts`, `objectql-strategy.ts`, `verify/README.md`) — each corrected a sentence the change made false, comment or README only; right, and the seat adopted them. (2) dead-code proof on the merged head, not `origin/main` — right (①(e)). (3) lock queue-timeouts — procedural. (4) `dashboard-window.ts`'s `$lte`-absent arms left (`selects`, `nestedIn`, the `to ?` spread, `fixtureDays`'s `end ?`) — dead on the head and harmless; deleting them is a comments-plus-code follow-up outside this card. Out-of-scope notes: `endExclusive` always true on the preset arm — true; the field stays load-bearing because the array arm emits `false` at every face (`memory-analytics.ts:1198`, `dataset-executor.ts:651`, `preview-evaluator.ts:632`). N+1 calendar days (`last_7_days` covers 8) — the ruled extent, the console's, pinned (spec day counts 8 / 31 / 91; executor `previousPeriod` 31 days). HTTP face with a future-dated row NOT MEASURED — accepted as declared (①(b)); a verify-family pin that writes one fixture after today would close it later.

Escalated by this record (not a dev flag): the ADR-0087 semantic entry in ①(d), outside every amended surface, so the seat amends the claim surface for it.

**Why FAIL.** One shipped sentence in the contract path leg still teaches the open window: `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.filter-preset-ordering-comparand-refused.ts:31-32` (`replacement`) says `{ $gte: "{30_days_ago}" }` is the window `last_30_days` means and what the rejection names; the head's rejection names `{ $between: ['{30_days_ago}', '{today}'] }`. The seat's own rule for this round (6142517145: published text this round makes false is fixed in this round) applies to it as it did to items a–g. Remedy, one patch round: (1) in that entry's `replacement`, change `{ $gte: "{30_days_ago}" } for last_30_days` to `{ $between: ["{30_days_ago}", "{today}"] } for last_30_days` (the entry's own double-quote spelling; nothing else in the entry; entry prose is scanned as source per the entries README, so keep it a quoted example); (2) in `.changeset/23170-rolling-presets-close-on-today.md`, add `'@objectstack/lint': patch` and `'@objectstack/verify': patch` and one sentence naming the entry correction; (3) seat amends the claim surface for the entry and re-renders this review at tier on the new head, where the DELIBERATE CORRECTION's confirmation is restated. Everything else judged above is right as it stands.
